record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e belongs to at least one positive circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: EP1. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a positive circle? Ans. Not known. This question is the negation of E5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma=(G,\sigma)$ consisting of a finite undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ together with a sign function $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$. A circle (also called a cycle or circuit) in $\Sigma$ is a connected 2-regular subgraph; its sign is defined to be the product $\prod_{e\in C}\sigma(e)$ of the signs of its edges. A circle is called positive if its sign equals $+1$, and negative otherwise.

Design an algorithm (and determine its computational complexity) for the following decision problem:

Given a signed graph $\Sigma=(G,\sigma)$ and a distinguished edge $e\in E(G)$, decide whether there exists a positive circle of $\Sigma$ containing the edge $e$.

In particular, determine whether this problem is solvable in polynomial time, is NP-complete, or has some intermediate complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of deciding whether a given edge of a signed graph lies on some positive circle is listed as not known in the standard problem collection on negative/positive circles in signed graphs. The complexity status (polynomial-time solvable vs. NP-complete) appears to remain open; related variants for induced positive/negative circles are also open and conjectured to be NP-complete.

status_evidence.title: Negative (and positive) circles in signed graphs: A problem collection
status_evidence.snippet: EP1. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a positive circle? Ans. Not known.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of deciding whether an edge belongs to a positive circle in a signed graph is listed as not known.

status_evidence.title: Negative (and positive) circles in signed graphs: A problem collection (Tandfonline)
status_evidence.snippet: Questions about whether a given edge belongs to a positive or negative (induced) circle are in NP, with complexity status not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of the edge-in-positive-circle decision problem is not resolved in the literature.
